newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine customs head removed amid graft probe.
newsitem.headline: Argentine customs head removed amid graft probe.

text.p: Argentine customs service administrator Juan Carlos Tomasetti Friday was removed from his post, an Economy Ministry spokesman said.

The spokesman who made the announcement to reporters gave no reason for the move. But the customs service is being investigated due to a series of corruption and smuggling scandals which the government estimates has cost it $3 billion in uncollected tariffs in the past four years.

Tomasetti was confirmed in his post as customs administrator in November by Carlos Silvani, the new head of the tax collection agency DGI after the customs and DGI were merged and Silvani made their overall head.
But Friday Tomasetti, who headed the customs service for more than one year, was replaced by Maria Isabel Fantelli, who had been in charge of the customs judicial affairs office.
Tomasetti will be made an undersecretary working in the sale of state-owned property, the ministry spokesman said.

On Thursday a prosecutor said authorities had arrested six people and were searching for 18 others in connection with a ring that smuggled in 40 tonnes of cameras, surgical instruments, perfume and electronics from the United States this year.
And earlier this week congressmen probing a huge customs fraud discovered 1.5 tonnes of cocaine in safety deposit boxes rented by the customs service in the National Bank.

Members of the lower house's investigative committee said the confiscated drugs, with a street value of $150 million, should have been burned five days after seizure but some had been there in bags and suitcases since 1984.
Some committee members criticized Tomasetti at the time, saying he had failed to inform about the existence of the deposit boxes.
